Display Energy Certs (DEC’s) were completed for 7

energy performance and carbon emissions of the building 
over a 12-month period. It includes recommendations on 
actions to reduce energy and emissions and must be 
displayed in a prominent position in the building to raise 
awareness.   
 
 
Energy Audits  
Energy Audits were completed for 3 Council Buildings including the Road Design Office (No. 1 Dean Street), 
KRSP Office (No. 5 Dean Street) and the Carnegie Library.  The audits examine the building fabric, heating 
systems, internal lighting and energy cost and consumption for a 12-month period and make 
recommendations on actions to reduce energy and emissions.  
The findings of the Energy Audits are used to develop a list of priority projects for the Council which when 
implemented will help us to achieve our statutory emissions and energy reductions targets.

A series of Free Electrical Recycling Days took place throughout the Month of August in Kilkenny. This was 
a collaborative program between the Environment Department of Kilkenny County Council and WEEE 
Ireland as well as our local community and Tidy Towns organisations.  Any household waste electrical items,

to power tools and everything in-between. 
Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny 
 
 
This year’s “Team Up to Clean Up” took place from the 20th to 22nd September, 2024 led by Kilkenny 
County Council in a collaborative effort to promote environmental stewardship, leading sponsors including 
Dawn Meats, Tirlán/Glanbia Plc, Panda, PRL and the John O’Shea Trust joined forces to support this 
essential community initiative.  
Over the course of the weekend, over 120 registered groups participated with an estimated 4,000 
enthusiastic volunteers engaged in litter picking across the County reinforcing the community’s commitment 
to maintaining a clean and vibrant environment. This included 35 schools across the City and County.   
Volunteers not only contributed to a cleaner environment but also became ambassadors for sustainable 
practices that mitigate littering in the long term.

8 
 
 
As part of the “Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny” Campaign for 2024, 20 primary and secondary 
schools involved in the Green Schools Programme have registered to participate in the award-winning 
Composting and Recycling for Schools Programme. 
The aim of the programme is to help schools prevent waste, improve recycling and set up, start or improve 
on-site composting systems to reduce waste, save money and combat climate change. The programme 
also helps schools improve their gardening efforts and increase biodiversity around their schools.  All of 
these activities assist schools with attaining their Green School Flags and reaching their Sustainable 
Development Goals.  In addition, the programme gives teachers access to a wide variety of fun, participatory 
and interactive activities for school children to learn about waste prevention, recycling, composting and 
gardening. These activities support children’s understanding of the underlying principles of ecology, biology 
and biodiversity that underpin all life on our planet. 
 
Each participating school will receive a €250 voucher to spend on in-school collection caddies, indoor 
recycling bins, instructional signs, a variety of composting systems, including composting bins, leaf mould 
cages and wormeries, and composting tools, including secateurs, pitch forks, compost aerators, watering 
cans, thermometers and anything that supports their respective action plans.

Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 46 Bring Centers across the City and County.  A total of 1550 tonnes 
of recyclables were collected from our Bring Centers to date in 2024.  This represents a 1% from the same 
period in 2023. Loughboy Shopping Centre - Kilkenny City (14 tonnes collected), Aldi - Kilkenny City (13 
tonnes collected), Lidl - Johnswell, Kilkenny City (8 tonnes collected) and are the busiest locations in the 
City. Aldi - Ferrybank (9 tonnes collected), Lidl - Thomastown (7 tonnes collected) and Graiguemanagh (6 
tonnes collected) are the busiest outside of the City.  Environment staff are continuing to work very closely 
with our service providers to ensure the collection service is in keeping with demand, especially around long 
weekends and holiday periods.

Noise 
Kilkenny County Council with support of Noise Consultants Limited have completed the draft Noise Action 
Plan 2024-2028. The draft Noise Action Plan is aimed at strategic long-term management of environmental 
noise from major roads. It does not apply to noise from domestic activities, neighbourhood noise, noise at 
workplaces or noise inside means of transport or due to military activities in military areas.  
The plan is now at the public consultation stage between 30th October and 11th of November 2024 with 
submissions being accepted until 25th November 2024. The final plan is on target to be submitted to the 
EPA in December 2024.

Lacken Boardwalk Enhancement Scheme 
Works continue to progress on the Lacken Boardwalk with circa. 75% of the works now completed. 
Unfortunately, the wet summer and subsequent poor ground conditions has delayed the completion date by

Clover Centre Ferrybank 
In late 2023 Kilkenny County Council took possession of circa. 9.5 acres of land, which includes sports 
pitches and a clubhouse from the trustees of Clover Meats in Christendom, Ferrybank, South Kilkenny.  A 
condition attached to this land transfer was that same could only be used for the recreational use of the 
community. 
The Council has identified the need to engage the services of a multidisciplinary landscape architecture & 
engineering led design team to prepare a masterplan for the future development of a high quality, community 
centred and multifunctional local park on this site. To this end, a tender for the above services was 
advertised on e-tenders in September and the deadline for tender submissions is set for the 23rd October 
2024.

11 
 
 
The development of the Masterplan will be undertaken in a collaborative approach with the local community 
through extensive public consultation to identify local community needs, priorities and desires. The overall 
objective of this initiative is to develop a high-quality parkland that will attract not just locals but visitors from 
the wider urban and rural catchment. It is our desire that the Park, when complete, will support the role of 
Ferrybank to achieve a more balanced Waterford City on both sides of the River Suir creating a space that 
offers quality of life improvements in terms of physical and mental health wellbeing and returning this area 
once again to a hub for social interaction.  
Playgrounds 
Ongoing maintenance continues around the County in our playgrounds and parks to maintain them to a 
high standard.  This month the focus was on the replacement of parts of old or worn play equipment and re-
mulching. In Ferrybank Neighbourhood Park footpath rehabilitation works were progressed with same

Amenity Grants 
In 2024, 175 applicants under the Amenity Grant scheme were awarded funding totalling €140,000.  This 
funding enabled groups across the County to maintain their own outdoor recreational spaces.  The range of 
works typically involve tree planting, grass cutting, planting flowers and many other amenity type projects.  
Successful applicants were required to submit documentation (receipts in respect of expenses incurred and 
photographs of completed projects) to claim their grants by 27th September, 2024. Grants are currently 
being processed. 
Tree Surgery 
Our annual Tree Surgery Works Programme recently recommenced. The focus will be on crown reductions 
and the removal of branches where there is a particular safety concern of where such interventions will help 
to prolong the life of a tree. In certain circumstances the removal of trees can’t unfortunately be avoided, 
however, it is proposed that compensatory planting will be undertaken later on in the year within the Kilkenny 
Countryside Park, Woodstock, Ferrybank Playground, and Slieverue Linear Park. 
2023 Local Biodiversity Action Fund 
Over the next month, major work will be carried out in Woodstock to remove invasive species such as Cherry 
Laurel, Rhododendron Ponticum, and Himalayan Honeysuckle at the Waterfall Trail and between the Noble 
Fir and Monkey Puzzle avenues within the gardens. This project, along with removal of Himalayan Balsam 
earlier in the year in Sliaire Wood, Graiguenamanagh is being funded under the Local Biodiversity Action 
Fund. 
Woodstock Gardens and Arboretum 
Our new autumn campaign for Woodstock Gardens and Arboretum was launched in September with the 
tagline “Wander Through the Seasons.” This campaign will market the gardens and woodlands, showcasing 
the fantastic walks and trails where visitors can enjoy the stunning autumn colours of the trees in Woodstock.

requisite documents to complete their applications subject to them meeting the qualifying criteria.  Full 
information is available at  https://kilkennycoco.ie/affordable-homes

as applicants will be required to demonstrate their capacity to purchase. Only valid applications (i.e. 
applications with all required documentation submitted) will go forward for assessment. Applications which

Time receiving social housing supports: The period of time tenants will be required to be in receipt of 
social housing support to be considered eligible under the scheme remains at 10 consecutive years.

A Social Farming open day took place at Éiru Farm, Jerpoint, Thomastown on 24th September, 
2024.  Social Farming Projects in Kilkenny are supported by the Local Community Development 
Committee (LCDC) through the Healthy Ireland Fund.  These projects provide individuals with 
additional needs the opportunity to spend time on a family farm in a welcoming, supportive, and 
inclusive environment.  Participants can engage in a variety of activities that interest them, such as 
gardening, animal care, or indoor tasks like baking bread or making jam. 
Activities are tailored to suit each person's abilities and preferences, ensuring a safe and 
encouraging atmosphere. The focus is on helping participants build confidence, develop social 
connections, and form meaningful relationships. While the farm is a typical working farm, not a 
treatment facility, it offers a non-clinical space where individuals can benefit from the positive 
experiences of farm life.
